title: fix(cli)!: refuse a production os serve that composes no organization object, --server or not
body:
Fixes #25133

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

Executes the maintainer's ruling 6328987873 (letter A) under the claim 6329345390. Dispatched by the epic seat (`epic:#15194`, `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3`). Ships as an 18.x patch. Review tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, because the diff declares a narrowing.

## What changed

`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`: a production `os serve` / `os start` (no `--dev`) that composes no organization object is now refused **whether or not `--server`**, before any plugin starts:

- **The `auth` tier is off and no `AuthPlugin` is mounted (A1).** The condition goes from `flags.server && noAuth` to `(flags.server || !isDev) && noAuth`. A development boot keeps the old shape: it is refused only when it serves.
- **The tier is on but no secret resolved (`no-secret`).** The condition drops `flags.server`. `no-secret` is only ever the reason on a production boot, because a development boot resolves the fallback secret, so this needs no posture check of its own.
- **Both refusal texts** drop the "run with --no-server" remedy and the "drop the REST/dispatcher plugins" remedy. Both were offered as ways to serve without the data API, and both still write ownerless rows. Each text now says that kernel-only does not avoid the refusal. The no-secret text also names the migrate-and-exit job.
- **Unchanged:**
  - the `host-kernel` reason (the cloud runtime's warn-only path);
  - `os dev` and `--dev`;
  - programmatic embedding, which never runs this command.
- **Ruling item 2:** no "tenant-scoped objects present" qualifier is written. I measured no composition it would spare (see Acceptance notes).

## Ruling item 5: the count

15 test files name `--no-server`. 8 of them carry neither `--dev` nor an auth secret, not 9:

- **7 are unit-level** and boot nothing: `serve-datasource-admin-routes`, `serve-http-server-composition`, `serve-kernel-only-hold`, `serve-no-transport-announcements` (unit), `serve-observability-registration`, `serve-unknown-hostname-guard`, `format.server-ready-no-http-server`. Each reads `serve.ts` source or calls a pure function.
- **1 spawns, but not in production:** `serve-migrate-exit-schema-parity.integration`. It spawns through `bin/run-dev.js`, which pins `NODE_ENV=development`, so it is a dev boot and is untouched.

The one test that really boots production `--no-server` without a secret is `test/serve-ready-degraded-boot.e2e.test.ts` (nightly tier). It carries `OS_AUTH_SECRET` in its healthy leg only, which is why the flag/secret count misses it. Its degraded leg is re-fixtured onto the one production composition that still skips auth with a warning: a host-kernel stub, a plugin registered under `ObjectOSEnvironmentPlugin`'s name.

**Missed by that count, found by CI on `5996c531`:** four cli integration files booted production `--no-server --preset minimal`. `minimal` composes no auth (tiers `['core']`), so ruling item 1's no-auth refusal now reaches them: `serve-no-server-banner`, `serve-no-transport-announcements`, `serve-kernel-only-lifetime` and `serve-no-storage-boot-guard` (6 tests). They are re-fixtured in `6531b332`. The banner and transport legs boot today's production kernel-only command (auth composed, a store). The lifetime and no-storage legs, whose shape is no store and no auth, boot the host-kernel stub with tiers `['core','auth']` and still pass `--preset minimal`. **Consequence:** a production `os serve --preset minimal` is now refused with or without `--server`, unless the stack mounts AuthPlugin itself. It was already refused with `--server`. This is ruling item 1 as written (report 6330837413).

Non-test callers: no workflow, Dockerfile, example or script in the repo runs `--no-server`. `os start` always hands its `serve` child a secret.

## Pins: `packages/cli/test/serve-no-auth-secret-refusal.integration.test.ts` (10 legs)

All legs spawn `bin/run.js` with `NODE_ENV` unset.

- **Refused, with the database never opened:**
  - no-secret with `--server`;
  - no-secret with `--no-server`;
  - no-secret `--no-server` with `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1`;
  - no-auth with `--server`;
  - no-auth with `--no-server` (with a secret).
- **Boots, reaching ready and opening the database:**
  - a configured secret with `--server`;
  - a configured secret with `--no-server`;
  - `--dev --no-server` with no secret;
  - the host kernel with no secret, `--no-server` (asserts the warn-only line);
  - no-auth with `--dev --no-server`.

## Proof (head `6531b332`; CI green: 42 check runs, 0 failing, Test Core 6/6)

- **The changed files, locally:**
  - the pin file: 10/10;
  - `serve-ready-degraded-boot.e2e` (`OS_TEST_TIERS=nightly`): 2/2.
- **cli unit layer:** `vitest run --project unit` reports 321/321 files and 4746/4746 tests. Lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- **cli typecheck:** exit 0.
- **cli integration layer:** the rest of it is declared to CI (`Test Core`).
- **Ablation 1:** `ablation-replace.mjs` turns the no-secret condition back to `flags.server && …`, the cli is rebuilt, and `ablation-dist-preflight` confirms the marker is in `dist/`.
  - Result: 2 failed and 8 passed. The red pins are no-secret `--no-server` ("the boot was not refused") and the migrate-and-exit leg (it exited 0).
  - Restore: blob == HEAD.
- **Ablation 2:** the no-auth condition goes back to `flags.server && …`.
  - Result: 1 failed and 9 passed. The red pin is no-auth `--no-server`.
  - Restore: blob == HEAD. After a rebuild, `--absent` confirms both markers are gone from all 680 built files and the tree is clean.
- **`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`:** 101 families, every exit code captured before any pipe.
  - Five were non-zero on the first sweep: four prerequisite refusals (exit 3: a shallow clone, and unbuilt packages) and `check:cli-test-child-env` (exit 1, a real finding).
  - The finding is fixed in `5996c531`: `NODE_ENV: undefined` now sits after each leg's env spread.
  - All five re-ran at exit 0 after a full build and a fetch of the pinned fixture commit. `--ran` accounts for 101 of 101.
- **`check-governed-merges --branch`:** exit 0, NOT governed (0 of 6 paths), +276 / -63.
- **R1:**
  - `pnpm dev:crm -- --fresh` reached ready, health 200;
  - a production `os serve` of `examples/app-crm` with `OS_AUTH_SECRET` reached ready, health 200;
  - the same app with `--no-server` and no secret exits 1 with the new text, and its database is never opened.
- **R4:** a walled production `os serve` (`OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=group`, `invite-only`, `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`, a secret) on a scratch app that declares `@objectstack/organizations` reached ready with `Organizations` composed, health 200.

## Docs

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`: the `--no-server` example and the flag description now say a production kernel-only boot is held to the same auth rule.
- `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`: the 18.0 auth-secret paragraph now covers no-auth, `--no-server`, migrate-and-exit, and the unaffected boots.
- `content/docs/releases/**` is not touched (ruling item 4). The changeset carries the correction for the v18 page's `--no-server` sentence.

## Acceptance notes

- **The `tenancy.enabled: false` remedy was left out on purpose.** The dispatch asked for it as an operator remedy, but ruling item 2 writes no qualifier, so declaring it does not lift the no-auth refusal. Offering it in the refusal text would advertise a fix that does not work. The changeset says so explicitly.
- **The pending changeset `.changeset/24583-7b3-organizationless-counter-retired.md`** (already shipped in 18.0.0's `dist`, still pending in `.changeset/`) contradicts this change twice: "Unchanged: `--no-server` (kernel only) still boots with the warning" and "or run kernel-only with `--no-server`". It is outside the claimed file surface and was not edited. This PR's changeset states that it supersedes both sentences. The seat may want that file corrected before the next version cut.
- **The degraded-boot e2e's healthy and degraded legs** now differ in config (bare vs host-kernel stub) as well as secret. Its header says so.
- **The pin file now spawns 10 boots,** about 34 s of wall time locally. It declares no `test-budget:`, because there is no CI reading yet.
- **Edits were first made on the session's primary checkout** (the claim's "the cloud session's own checkout"). They moved to a linked worktree once the guard hooks refused; no content was lost.
